title: Event Sourcing

validation.research: Six primary sources: Martin Fowler’s Event Sourcing author catalog article, Microsoft’s Event Sourcing architecture guidance, EventSourcingDB Writing Events, Axon Snapshots, SQLite Transactions, and Python sqlite3. Canonical Event Sourcing is retained; event-sourced persistence is described as shorthand. Event-driven integration, an audit trail, CQRS, and authoritative event persistence are explicitly distinguished. Conditional append, schema compatibility, deterministic replay, external effects, projection lag, checkpoints, correction semantics, and operating costs are treated separately. The article does not infer automatic throughput gains, universal global ordering, or automatic deduplication from append-only storage.

runnable_example.verification: Exact demo output; reconstruction at revisions two and three; retained earlier prefix unchanged; repeated pure replay with file/database I/O forbidden; no history mutation; close/reopen recovery from authoritative events alone; expected-revision rejection adds nothing; insufficient-capacity and reservation-aware over-release rejection; stream isolation; application update/delete trigger rejection; unknown schema/type, broken order, and invalid fixed-v1 facts fail visibly; exact 1/1000-seat and 64/65-character ID boundaries; invalid inputs leave no event; two concurrent revision-one writers yield one append and one conflict, with losing command re-evaluated against capacity; forced after-insert failure rolls back; busy-BEGIN and failed-COMMIT propagate with rollback and later retry; abrupt process exit before commit preserves earlier stream; newly versioned retries intentionally are not deduplicated. No authentication, external notification, asynchronous projection, schema migration, or production power-loss guarantee is inferred.

example_limits: Original two-file Python 3.11+ standard-library SQLite example. One event per command and full fixed-v1 replay validate the reservation-aware twenty-seat history. Stream positions start at one and the pool/revision pair supplies local event identity. BEGIN IMMEDIATE serializes SQLite writers before the expected-revision check; INSERT and check are in one transaction, and acknowledgment returns after commit. Replay interprets retained facts without I/O and does not create notifications. Application triggers prevent accidental UPDATE/DELETE but are not an administrator security or tamper-resistance boundary. No authentication, request deduplication, outbox, asynchronous projection, snapshot, event migration, encryption, backup/restore workflow, cross-stream atomicity, or production power-loss guarantee. A retry with a new expected revision can append a second legitimate-looking reservation. Independent concurrent writers, statement and commit failures, busy BEGIN, abrupt pre-commit process exit, invalid histories, over-release/capacity boundaries, and reopen reconstruction are verified.
